part5.question: Meals at Moonlight Grill consist of various dishes ------- for guests of all ages.
part5.explanation: An adjective is needed after the noun 'dishes' in a reduced relative clause ('dishes that are enjoyable for guests'). (C) 'enjoyable' is the adjective form, whereas (A) and (B) are finite verbs and (D) 'enjoying' cannot describe food.

part5.question: Mayberry Research Institute offers staff ------- which include dental coverage and a pension plan.
part5.explanation: After 'offers staff,' a plural countable noun is required as the direct object and antecedent of the plural verb 'include.' (C) 'benefits' is the plural noun meaning employee perks, while (A) is a verb, (B) an adverb, and (D) an adjective.

part5.question: Arranging an appointment to see Dr. Menard one month in advance is ------- due to her busy schedule.
part5.explanation: Because Dr. Menard has a busy schedule, scheduling an appointment a month early is required, making the adjective (D) 'necessary' the only logical fit among the choices.

part5.question: Patrons who had their vehicles parked waited by the Canton Theater entrance while ------- retrieved their cars.
part5.explanation: After 'while,' a plural noun subject is needed to perform the action 'retrieved their cars.' (C) 'attendants' (parking valets) fits both grammar and meaning, unlike the abstract noun 'attendance' or verb forms (A) and (B).

part5.question: ------- all the entrepreneurs in Florida are in favor of the government's plan to cut taxes, though a small minority is opposed.
part5.explanation: Because the second clause contrasts with 'though a small minority is opposed,' an adverb meaning 'almost' is needed to modify 'all.' (D) 'Nearly' ('nearly all') matches the exception, whereas 'Solely,' 'Certainly,' and 'Unusually' contradict it.

part5.question: AEG Co. is looking for sales associates who demonstrate excellent communication skills and an ability to work in a ------- manner.
part5.explanation: An adjective is needed between the article 'a' and the noun 'manner' to describe how associates work. (A) 'cooperative' is the adjective form, while (B) is a noun, (C) an adverb, and (D) a verb.

part5.question: The unnecessary extra work on Sackler Department Store's new building could have been ------- if the design plans had been followed precisely.
part5.explanation: In the conditional passive 'could have been + past participle,' the context describes unnecessary extra work that would have been prevented if plans were followed. (A) 'avoided' fits both the passive grammar and intended meaning.

part5.question: Ms. Herrera could not sit in an aisle seat during her international flight because there were ------- available.
part5.explanation: After 'there were,' a pronoun meaning 'not any' is required to explain why she could not sit in an aisle seat. (D) 'none' functions as that pronoun, whereas 'hardly' and 'mainly' are adverbs and 'any' is ungrammatical in an affirmative clause.

part5.question: Mr. Holt's acceptance of the financial executive position is ------- his satisfaction with the salary offer.
part5.explanation: Following 'is' and preceding the noun phrase 'his satisfaction,' an adjective + preposition phrase expressing condition is required. (B) 'dependent on' fits grammatically and logically, whereas 'in contrast to'/'as opposed to' signal contrast and 'on condition that' requires a full clause.

part5.question: Transport officials are still unsure of ------- caused Train 580 to break down earlier this morning.
part5.explanation: The preposition 'of' takes a noun clause in which the wh-word acts as the subject of 'caused.' (C) 'what' ('the thing that') fills the subject role, whereas 'why' is an adverb and 'each'/'those' cannot introduce a clause.

part5.question: The Project Green report argues ------- that the best way to save endangered species is by placing them in protected wildlife areas.
part5.explanation: An adverb is needed immediately after the verb 'argues' to modify how the report makes its case. (D) 'persuasively' is the adverb form, while (A) is an adjective, (B) a verb, and (C) a noun.

part5.question: The guide told visitors touring the High Point Library that the facility ------- by the renowned architect Albert Grand.
part5.explanation: Because the library received the design action (indicated by 'by the renowned architect Albert Grand') prior to the tour, a simple past passive verb is required. (B) 'was designed' provides the correct tense and passive voice.

part5.question: Sundersen Technologies ------- 10 percent from Mr. Garrison's bill since he was eligible for a bulk purchase discount.
part5.explanation: Because Mr. Garrison qualified for a bulk discount, the company subtracted 10 percent from his bill. (A) 'deducted' collocates naturally with 'from' and fits the meaning, unlike 'substituted,' 'deposited,' or 'submitted.'

part5.question: ------- the recent economic upturn, unemployment is on the decline as more and more businesses are hiring full-time employees.
part5.explanation: Before the noun phrase 'the recent economic upturn,' a causal preposition is needed to show why unemployment is declining. (B) 'As a result of' takes a noun phrase and expresses cause, whereas 'Despite' signals contrast and 'In order that'/'Provided that' take full clauses.

part5.question: Passengers ------- to fill in their arrival forms during the flight for quicker processing at the immigration checkpoint.
part5.explanation: 'Passengers' are the recipients of the reminder, requiring a present passive verb followed by the infinitive 'to fill in.' (D) 'are reminded' expresses this routine passenger instruction accurately.

part5.question: Overdrive is a low-budget action film that has no ------- to actor Sam Horton's autobiography, which has the same title.
part5.explanation: After the determiner 'no' and before 'to,' a noun is required in the expression 'have no relation to' ('have no connection with'). (D) 'relation' is the noun form, while (A), (B), and (C) are verb or adjective forms.

part5.question: Without exception, ------- employees must undergo on-the-job training to enhance their skills.
part5.explanation: With 'Without exception' and the plural noun 'employees,' a universal plural quantifier is needed. (B) 'all' modifies plural 'employees' directly, whereas 'every' requires a singular noun, 'a lot' needs 'of,' and 'few' contradicts 'Without exception.'

part5.question: The client was never in his office ------- many times Ms. Baxter tried to call him.
part5.explanation: The structure '[conjunctive adverb] + many + noun' meaning 'no matter how many times' requires (B) 'however.' The other choices ('otherwise,' 'hence,' 'somehow') cannot modify 'many' to form a concessive clause.

part5.question: LocerTech's primary goal is to be as ------- as possible to customer inquiries.
part5.explanation: Inside 'as [adjective] as possible to customer inquiries,' an adjective meaning 'quick to answer' that pairs with 'to' is needed. (C) 'responsive' fits both the 'responsive to' collocation and customer-service context.

part5.question: Rodgers Industrial celebrated the ------- of its 50th anniversary by hosting a banquet for clients from around the world.
part5.explanation: After 'celebrated the' and before 'of its 50th anniversary,' a noun meaning a milestone event is required. (C) 'occasion' fits naturally, whereas 'impression,' 'integration,' and 'gratitude' do not match celebrating an anniversary.

part5.question: Gilbot Grounds had to work ------- to get the landscaping project finished by the deadline.
part5.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the verb 'work' and describe the effort required to meet the deadline. (B) 'intensely' is the adverb form, while 'intense' and 'intensive' are adjectives and 'intensity' is a noun.

part5.question: Under the finance minister's leadership, corporations recovered quickly from last year's losses and then began making substantial -------.
part5.explanation: Contrasting with 'last year's losses' and following 'making substantial,' a noun meaning profits is needed. (B) 'earnings' fits both the contrast and the collocation 'making earnings,' unlike 'regulations,' 'entrants,' or 'estimations.'

part5.question: The provision of additional government grants for college tuition will make education ------- to more people from around the country.
part5.explanation: Additional tuition grants enable more students to obtain an education, requiring an adjective meaning 'obtainable/reachable' that pairs with 'to.' (D) 'accessible' completes 'make education accessible to more people.'

part5.question: The current edition of the employee handbook ------- detailed guidelines for employee performance reviews.
part5.explanation: The singular subject 'The current edition' requires a third-person singular present verb in the active voice. (C) 'contains' agrees with the singular subject, whereas (A) is plural, (B) is passive, and (D) is a participle without a finite verb.

part5.question: Shoppers looking for high-quality electronics at low prices will find a ------- selection at the new NorvelTech store.
part5.explanation: An adjective is needed between 'a' and 'selection'; because the indefinite article 'a' precludes a superlative here, the comparative adjective (D) 'greater' ('a larger selection') is correct, while 'greatly' is an adverb and 'greaten' is a verb.

part5.question: Although Southmoore Records has been actively seeking a new CEO for three months, they have ------- to find a suitable candidate.
part5.explanation: The fixed expression 'have yet to + base verb' means 'still have not.' (A) 'yet' completes this idiom to express the contrast introduced by 'Although,' whereas 'never,' 'seldom,' and 'seemed' do not fit the structure or context.

part5.question: Many office workers frequent Stan's Bistro because of its ------- to the business district.
part5.explanation: To explain why office workers visit the bistro often, a noun meaning 'nearness' that collocates with 'to' is needed. (A) 'proximity' ('proximity to the business district') fits both meaning and preposition usage.

part5.question: The temperature this morning is cool and pleasant, but it is expected to increase steadily ------- the day.
part5.explanation: To describe a continuous temperature increase from morning across the entire day, a preposition of duration meaning 'from start to finish of' is required. (D) 'throughout' fits 'throughout the day,' unlike 'between,' 'above,' or 'next to.'

part5.question: Now that the city has hired additional workers, it can ------- with the construction of the new civic center.
part5.explanation: After the modal 'can' and before 'with the construction,' an intransitive verb meaning 'go ahead/continue' is needed. (D) 'proceed' pairs directly with 'with' ('proceed with construction'), unlike 'enhance,' 'concern,' or 'replace.'

part5.question: ------- to be the best in the city, the Melise Restaurant is booked for the next six months.
part5.explanation: This sentence begins with a reduced passive participle clause ('Because it is reported to be the best in the city...'). (C) 'Reported' provides the past participle needed for the passive meaning.

To: All staff members
From: Greg Birch, CTO

options.D: Several companies in the affected area reported similar outages.

passages.title: The Regency Scotia School of Design Hosts Historic Royal Costume Display
passages.content:
Threads of Royal History, launched on Friday, is the latest exhibit from the Regency Scotia School of Design (RSSD) in Glasgow. It is a treat for period costume enthusiasts. For the exhibit, the school borrowed 52 outfits belonging to both historical and current monarchs from museums around the world. Of particular note are the 4,000 year old headdress and accessories on loan from the Cairo Museum in Egypt as well as several stunning robes from the Forbidden City Museum in Beijing. In addition, fashion students from the school have created 38 replica outfits. All of the items are beautifully displayed on specially designed mannequins.

The exhibit will last for a month, concluding on April 30. Regular admission is £6.50, but students and faculty of the RSSD are admitted for free. Senior citizens pay £5.00, and children 10 and under pay £3.50. Inquire about student group rates by calling 555-3400. The exhibit space is located in the school's Leighton Hall, which is open from 10 A.M. through 8 P.M., Monday through Thursday.

passages.title: USER REVIEW: Wheel-Pals Carpooling Application
passages.content:
USER REVIEW: Wheel-Pals Carpooling Application
By Jason Diaz (jdiaz@vastpost.co.au)
Rating: 4/5 stars (★★★★☆)

Wheel-Pals recently launched its service in the Auckland area, and having already used the application while living in Brisbane, I was one of the first to sign up. As before, I purchased the basic package because, in the past, it had enough services to help me form carpool groups with other drivers or riders that live nearby. However, I don't think Wheel-Pals has done enough to promote its launch in this area. I sometimes find it difficult to find people to carpool with. In Brisbane, I only drove my car to work once or twice a week, but now I have to do it more often. Also, few people that I know locally are even aware of the application.

passages.title: Spartan Tires Joins Forces with Maha-Rubber
passages.content:
By Enid Wendall

Spartan Tires announced in a press statement yesterday that it will finalize a deal with India-based manufacturer Maha-Rubber on June 18. The company will produce tires under the Spartan Tires brand. Spartan Tires has 38 branches across the country, with an average of four new franchises opening annually. However, it does not produce its own accessories or parts, carrying only those made by other companies. Spartan Tires CEO Carlo Gregario said in the statement, "We don't have the facilities to produce our own tires. Partnering with Maha-Rubber will allow us to do so at a reasonable cost." The first of the new products will be available at Spartan Tires retail outlets nationwide on August 1 of next year.
